papers.text: A motorway bench for watching coaches. Where the hedge is now.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: The National Clock back an hour on show day: growers need more time. Spotters, less.
papers.subject: clocks

papers.text: Turn the street lamps to the shop windows. Then the bus stop's. Then the lighthouse.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: Your second telephone, please. The League rings it 40 times a day.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Tune a foghorn to the band. Then all of them. Then book a fog.
papers.subject: harbours

papers.text: Give the marrows the band's Sunday. They are licensed to perform.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: A bandstand on wheels. We were told to go where the audience is: the kites.
papers.subject: inventions

papers.text: Till's Teas will sponsor the lamps, if they glow tea-coloured. Milky.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: Pose with our ten-thousandth coach. It will not be stopping.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: An arcade sign: PRIZE PUMPKIN, THIS WAY. It points outside.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: Band practice on the motorway bridge? Sunday is rare-coach day.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: A spotting platform by the motorway. The bank is 80 % onion.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Kites get the harbour wall. Anglers may apply to sit on the water.
papers.subject: harbours

papers.text: Cushion the harbour wall, for the echo. Then the bandstand. Then the band.
papers.subject: harbours

papers.text: The hedge show, on the kite field. Kites that land get clipped.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: Hear the band down the third telephone, for the camera. Nod.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: A meter on our lake, counting the growers' watering cans. By hand.
papers.subject: inventions

papers.text: Lamp-post signs: KITES MAY REST HERE. Guild baskets to budge up.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: Trim the arcade hedge. Then the awnings, to match. Then the hats.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: Dim the Guild's harbour windows at dusk. The water is 40 % hat.
papers.subject: harbours

papers.text: The band will hire a lighthouse for a concert. The tunes go round.
papers.subject: harbours

papers.text: Unhook the telephones for the Quiet Competition. Till's Teas keeps trying.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: We will pay for a hedge down the motorway. Spotters lose the far side.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: Walk the arcade with the band, carrying the cymbals. Carrying only.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: A landing circle by the marrows. Kites miss circles by 3 metres.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: We will pay to name a junction after the pumpkin. Then the rest. Spotters liked numbers.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: Launch a kite named after you. Smile before it finds the hedge.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: We will sponsor the National Clock's quietest minute. Band to rest. Plaque: SHH.
papers.subject: clocks

papers.text: A study: is a coach late if nobody waits for it? The Guild is asked to wait.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The study asks the Guild to wait at a second stop, as a control.

papers.text: Your face on the National Clock. At noon both hands point at you.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: A study of marrows by lamplight. Half the high street goes dark, as a control.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The marrow study needs the dark half lit again, and the lit half dark.

papers.text: A desk lamp. It glows near ribbons. Any openings soon? No reason.
papers.subject: ribbons

favour.text: About the lamp: it would like a solo at the Sunday concert.

clippings.sign: PRESIDENT'S LAMP GIVEN SOLO; BAND PLAYS IN THE DARK
clippings.refuse: LAMP STAYS ON THE DESK, GLOWING AT NOTHING

papers.text: Switch on the night hedge show. Stand by the switch. Look pleased.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: A study on dressing the lighthouse window. So far, all Till's Teas.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The lighthouse study now wishes to dress the beam. Stripes, alternately.

papers.text: A lighthouse to flash your initials. Then your name. Then speeches.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: A study: is a humming kite an instrument? Bring kites.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The kite study asks to hear a whistling kite, and one that sighs.

papers.text: A plaque on each lamp: LIT BY THE PRESIDENT. I have done four.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: A study: is the anglers' willow a hedge? If so, it gets trimmed.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The willow study asks to inspect every willow. Shears packed.

papers.text: Three small umbrellas, one per telephone. Say 'rain' more often?
papers.subject: vanity

favour.text: About the umbrellas: they wish to judge the marrow show. Open.

clippings.sign: PRESIDENT'S UMBRELLA JUDGES MARROWS; GROWERS DAMP
clippings.refuse: UMBRELLAS STAY BY THE TELEPHONES, OPINIONS UNSHARED

papers.text: A study of awnings kites land on. So far, 9 in 10 prefer stripes.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The awning study asks to try plain awnings too. And spots.
